about: Each record a probe writes differently on the asset bundle's base than on the oracle's installation, by fixture, with its reason (kb/topics/asset-bundle.md). Held by crates/winbox-win16/tests/assets_sweep.rs and test/assets/sweep_test.ts (ASSETS_SWEEP=1): a difference not listed fails, and so does one listed that no longer comes. A record is `function(args)`, or ends in `*` for every record it begins; `stop` is how the run ended. `engine`, where given, is the one engine the entry is for. `corpus`: each program whose calls or screens differ on the base from the TypeScript engine's survey on the installation (`examples/corpus.rs --base assets`), with why.

corpus.wslam: Imports COMMDLG: on the installation COMMDLG.DLL is loaded and its LibEntry's calls (LocalInit, ...) come first; on the base COMMDLG is WinBox's own, with no code to run, and the calls part at the first
corpus.hanoi: Imports COMMDLG: COMMDLG.DLL's LibEntry runs first on the installation, not on the base. The same calls, and the same run, on the installation with COMMDLG.DLL taken off
corpus.fibsw: Imports COMMDLG: COMMDLG.DLL's LibEntry runs first on the installation, not on the base
corpus.wordsrch: Imports COMMDLG: COMMDLG.DLL's LibEntry runs first on the installation, not on the base
corpus.champ: Imports COMMDLG: COMMDLG.DLL's LibEntry runs first on the installation, not on the base
corpus.caribb: Imports VER and DDEML: on the installation VER.DLL, LZEXPAND.DLL (which VER.DLL imports) and DDEML.DLL are loaded, their LibEntries run before the program and their segments take selectors; on the base all three are WinBox's own -- the calls part at the first, and GetDOSEnvironment answers another selector. The same on the installation with the three files taken off
corpus.bg: LoadLibrary(commdlg.dll): on the installation COMMDLG.DLL's file is loaded, on the base WinBox's own COMMDLG, so the module handle answered differs (478 there, 158 on the base) and the calls after it
corpus.simtower: Imports COMMDLG: on the 256-colour installation COMMDLG.DLL is loaded and its LibEntry allocates before the program runs, so the program's first GlobalAlloc answers another handle (1062 there, 990 on the base); the run parts from there, and the steps' screens are not reached where the report's were (WING is WinBox's own on both)

associco.reason: NOTEPAD.EXE, PROGMAN.EXE, MORICONS.DLL, WIN.COM and SYSTEM\USER.EXE are not on the base: SHELL gives its own icon 6, as for C:\NOPE.EXE, which is on neither; the .TXT files' program, notepad.exe, is not there either; and ExtractIcon of NOTEPAD.EXE gives no icon for DumpIcon

cardview.reason: CARDFILE.EXE is not on the base: WinExec answers 2, and there is no Cardfile to read

diskfree.reason: The TypeScript harness puts the base on a FAT16 volume it makes in memory, as the page makes its drive (fillDrive), where the installation is its own disk image: GetDiskFreeSpace of C: answers that volume's clusters, not the image's. A matter of the volume, not of the files on it; the Rust engine's host folders answer alike

filedlg.reason: C:\WINDOWS on the base has no .TXT file (SETUP.TXT, which Setup copies, and BOOTLOG.TXT, which WIN.COM writes as Windows starts): the dialog's file list is empty, so there is no file to click

freelib.reason: MAIN.CPL is not in the base's SYSTEM: LoadLibrary answers 2, and the rest is never reached

mapcpl.reason: MIDIMAP.DRV is not on the base: WinBox's mapper has no applet without it (CPL_INIT answers nought, `wbmapper/applet.rs`), so no dialog, the current setup is not changed, and the mapper opens on the installation's own setup's channels

verinfo.reason: COMMDLG.DLL, USER.EXE, GDI.EXE, SHELL.DLL, MMSYSTEM.DLL, SYSTEM.DRV, NOTEPAD.EXE, PROGMAN.EXE and CALC.EXE are not on the base, and the probe's VCOPY.DRV and VCOPY.DR_ are copies of SYSTEM.DRV: no version information. Its block left as it filled it (0CCh), the probe's own sum then reads 0CCCCh bytes of its 4100-byte block: a general protection fault, and the run ends there
The Rust engine's run: the fault's box of USER's, which no hand answers in the sweep, is still up when its time is up. The TypeScript harness tells no stop apart: its runs end alike on both

verinst.reason: SYSTEM.DRV is not on the base, and every source the probe makes is a copy of it, its version information changed; nor are SYSTEM\USER.EXE, SYSTEM\GDI.EXE, NOTEPAD.EXE and SYSTEM\COMMDLG.DLL, which VerFindFile and VerInstallFile look for
